Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

reactableEdit 0.4.5.9000 (Unreleased)

Fork

  • Renamed the R package to reactableEdit, an independent fork of Greg Lin’s reactable, maintained by Samuel JOBERT under the MIT license. Load it with library(reactableEdit); existing R function names, widget bindings, JavaScript APIs, and reactable.* options are unchanged. Original authors, copyright notices, and third-party licenses are retained. Earlier release sections below describe upstream reactable history.

Documentation

  • Added a comprehensive editing guide covering native Shiny inputs, stable and custom IDs, modules, individual observers, native updaters, explicit server validation, disabled rules, row actions, rich tooltips, persistence and troubleshooting, with a complete runnable Shiny application.

New features

  • Native Shiny cell editing with colDef(editable = TRUE), six input types (text, number, select, checkbox, date, and textarea), stable row keys via reactable(rowId = ...), customizable input IDs, and explicit server acceptance or rejection via getReactableEdit() and resolveReactableEdit(). Accepted edits display a customizable status (editStatus), with a green tick for 2 seconds by default (editStatusDuration). Previous success and errors clear on new input. Columns can opt out of server validation with editValidation = FALSE without displaying a validation tick. Native input[[id]] observers and update*Input() functions work for mounted cells. Editing preserves table state and is initially limited to client-side Shiny tables without .subRows data.

  • Add and remove rows in Shiny with rowActions = list(add = TRUE, remove = TRUE). Handle server requests with getReactableRowAction() and supply complete rows using addReactableRow(), optionally overriding new cell input IDs. Appended rows remain visible outside sorting, filtering, grouping and pagination until full data replacement. Removal requires confirmation, notifies the server immediately, and can be disabled per row. Requires stable row keys and client-side tables without .subRows or Crosstalk data.

  • Rich noninteractive tooltips for cells, native editable inputs (including disabled inputs), and column headers via reactableTooltip(), colDef(tooltip = ..., headerTooltip = ...), and stable-key tooltips rules in reactable() and updateReactable(). Use updateReactableTooltip() to override a mounted input’s help by ID. Tooltips support hover, keyboard focus, Escape dismissal, viewport-aware positioning and custom CSS; rules and per-input overrides survive pagination, virtual scrolling and data replacement.

  • Disable native cell inputs by column with colDef(inputDisabled = TRUE), or by stable row key, column, and cell using disabledInputs in reactable() and updateReactable(). Cell exceptions can enable otherwise disabled inputs. Use updateReactableInput() or native input messages for mounted cells; external DOM changes such as shinyjs::disable() also persist across remounts. Disabling discards unsent drafts without interrupting pending server responses.

  • Experimental support for server-side data processing in Shiny apps. Use reactable(server = TRUE) to render a table using server-side data processing in Shiny. Server-side data processing requires the V8 package, which is not installed with reactable by default. (#22)

    library(shiny)
library(reactableEdit)

tbl <- reactable(
  mtcars,
  server = TRUE
)

ui <- fluidPage(
  reactableOutput("tbl")
)

server <- function(input, output) {
  output$tbl <- renderReactable({
    tbl
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)

  • reactable() gains a virtual argument to enable virtual scrolling. Virtual scrolling renders only the visible rows on screen, allowing you to scroll through large tables without performance issues. (#203)

    reactable(
  data.frame(x = 1:100000, y = rnorm(100000)),
  pagination = FALSE,
  virtual = TRUE,
  height = 500
)

  • New Reactable.toggleSortBy() and Reactable.setSortBy() methods in the JavaScript API to programmatically control column sorting. toggleSortBy() toggles sort on a single column (cycling between ascending and descending), while setSortBy() sets the full sort state declaratively. Also available via updateReactable(sortBy = ...) in Shiny. (#316, #322)

  • New Reactable.toggleRowSelected(), Reactable.setRowsSelected(), and Reactable.toggleAllRowsSelected() methods in the JavaScript API to programmatically control row selection. Additionally, rowInfo.toggleRowSelected() and cellInfo.toggleRowSelected() are now available in JavaScript render and style functions. (#322, #394, #412)

  • New Reactable.gotoPage() and Reactable.setPageSize() methods in the JavaScript API to change the current page or page size. (#322)

  • JSON serialization of data can now be customized using the reactable.json.func option. This is an experimental feature for advanced use only, and intentionally undocumented outside of NEWS. reactable may change how data is serialized between versions and does not guarantee stability. See reactableEdit:::toJSON as a reference for how data is currently serialized. (@khusmann, #415)

    Example usage:

    # Use yyjsonr as a faster alternative for JSON serialization. Note that this is not 1:1 consistent with
# jsonlite, and several edge cases are not handled here, including data frames with 1 row, datetimes, and NULLs.
options(reactable.json.func = function(x, ...) {
  result <- yyjsonr::write_json_str(
    x,
    opts = yyjsonr::opts_write_json(
      dataframe = "columns",
      auto_unbox = TRUE,
      num_specials = "string"
    )
  )
  class(result) <- "json"
  result
})

  • colDef() gains an initWidth argument to set a column’s initial width in pixels while keeping the column resizable. Unlike width, which sets a fixed width and disables resizing, initWidth only sets the starting width, so the column can still be resized within its minWidth and maxWidth. (@nteetor, #223, #374)

Minor improvements and bug fixes

  • Improved rendering performance for large tables.
  • Fixed inconsistent spacing between column group borders on resizable tables. (@wvictor14, #396)
  • Fixed JS() not working when htmlwidgets 1.6.3 or later is installed. (#348)
  • In reactableTheme(), stripedColor and highlightColor now work when using sticky columns. (@grcatlin, #401)
  • In Crosstalk tables, pagination no longer resets when selecting a row on a page greater than 1. (@msaltieri, #349)
  • In Shiny apps, tables now update correctly when reactive meta values change. (@khusmann, #416)
  • Fixed pagination showing incorrect page buttons (e.g., “1 2 3 4 5 NaN”) when using pagination = FALSE with showPagination = TRUE and filtering out all rows.

Breaking changes

  • Internet Explorer 11 (IE 11) is no longer supported.
  • core-js is no longer included in the HTML dependencies. This was required to support IE 11 and old versions of the RStudio Viewer. (#245)
  • meta is now converted to JavaScript in the same way as data, using reactable’s internal JSON serialization function rather than htmlwidgets’s JSON serialization function. This should only be a breaking change in rare cases, as the major difference is that numeric NA, NaN, Inf, and -Inf values are now serialized as strings and preserved, rather than always being converted to null. (@khusmann, #415)
